channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Sóstenes e Rogério Marinho deixam Congresso e devem ir à sede do PL após matéria do Intercept
item.description: Opposition leaders Sóstenes and Rogério Marinho left Congress and are expected to go to the PL headquarters following an Intercept report revealing alleged financing by Daniel Vorcaro, owner of Master, for a film about Jair Bolsonaro's life. The lawmakers avoided commenting on the matter at the request of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a pre-candidate for president.

item.title: Relação entre Flávio e Vorcaro precisa ser investigada a fundo. diz Uczai
item.description: Pedro Uczai (SC), leader of the PT in the Chamber of Deputies, called for a 'thorough' investigation into the relationship between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, and the owner of [name not specified in the content], alleging suspicious links that require rigorous scrutiny.

item.title: Dólar bate R$ 5 após reportagem vincular Daniel Vorcaro e Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The dollar rose nearly 2% to R$ 5 after The Intercept Brasil reported that presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro negotiated with former banker Daniel Vorcaro the payment of R$ 134 million to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro. The revelation sparked market concern, amplifying exchange rate volatility amid suspicions of private funds being used for electoral campaign purposes. The linkage between political figures and financial actors raised questions about transparency and potential violations of campaign finance laws.

item.title: Flávio pediu dinheiro a Vorcaro para custear filme de Jair Bolsonaro: ‘Estarei contigo sempre’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requested funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse', about the life of former president Jair Bolsonaro, with payments already made totaling up to US$ 10 million of a negotiated US$ 24 million. The messages and audio, released by Intercept Brasil and confirmed as authentic by Estadão, were extracted from Vorcaro’s phone during Operation Compliance Zero. Despite the evidence, Flávio denied the financing, calling the claims lies and insisting the funds were private.

item.title: Ligação entre Vorcaro e Flávio é “afetiva e promíscua”, afirma PT
item.description: The PT leader in the Chamber, Pedro Uczai, stated that the audio attributed to Flávio Bolsonaro reveals an 'affective and promiscuous' relationship with Daniel Vorcaro, in which the senator requested R$134 million to finance the film 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro. The PT has engaged lawyers to assess legal actions and is pushing for a CPI to investigate Banco Master, questioning the legality of the funds and the consistency of Flávio’s assets, such as a R$6 million mansion, with his declared income.

item.title: Áudio que liga Flávio a Vorcaro acirra ofensiva eleitoral de Lula
item.description: An audio attributed to Flávio Bolsonaro shows him negotiating with jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance a Bolsonaro family film, with $10.6 million transferred between February and May 2025. The PT used the case to reinforce its electoral offensive against the opposition in 2026, linking it to the Bolsonaro family's history and the Banco Master scandal, while Minister José Guimarães urged PF and Justice investigations. A Genial/Quaest poll shows Lula at 42% and Flávio at 41% in a potential runoff, reversing the senator's earlier lead.

item.title: Vorcaro pagou R$ 61 mi a Flávio para bancar filme de Bolsonaro, diz site
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for the Brazilian presidency, negotiated with Daniel Vorcaro, former founder of Banco Master, the transfer of US$24 million to finance the film 'Dark Horse', about the life of Jair Bolsonaro. R$61 million were effectively transferred between February and May 2025 through companies and funds linked to Bolsonaro family allies. The senator demanded overdue payments in a September 2025 audio, fearing that defaults would harm the film’s image and that of his father.

item.title: “Flávio é um bandido e a direita não pode ser refém”, diz Kataguiri
item.description: Deputy Kim Kataguiri accused Senator Flávio Bolsonaro of being a "bandit" after an audio surfaced in which the senator demanded payments from banker Daniel Vorcaro related to the production of the film "Dark Horse", about Jair Bolsonaro's political trajectory. Kataguiri stated that the right cannot be held hostage by such actions.

item.title: Medidas de governo Lula para combustíveis custam R$ 2,9 bi por mês
item.description: President Lula's government announced a provisional measure to subsidize gasoline and diesel using federal budget funds, with an estimated monthly cost of up to R$ 2.9 billion for two months, possibly extendable. The subsidy mirrors the reduction of federal taxes such as PIS/Pasep, Cofins, and Cide, and will be paid to producers and importers within 30 days, with discounts reflected in electronic invoices. Despite the significant expense, the government claims the measures will not create fiscal deficits or require tax increases.

item.title: Dólar volta a bater R$ 5 com cenário eleitoral, inflação nos EUA e reportagem sobre Flávio Bolsonaro e Daniel Vorcaro
item.description: The dollar hit R$ 5 following an Intercept Brasil report linking Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to banker Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master in a bid to raise R$ 134 million for a film about Jair Bolsonaro. The rally was amplified by strong Brazilian retail data, improved approval ratings for Lula in the Genial/Quaest poll, and higher-than-expected U.S. producer inflation, which fueled expectations of further Federal Reserve rate hikes. The Ibovespa fell 1.46% to 177,713 points, while long-term interest rate futures rose sharply, with the January 2029 DI contract at 14.075% and the 2033 contract at 14.20%.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio Bolsonaro estão desnorteados
item.description: The few allies of Flávio Bolsonaro who are still answering calls following the Intercept Brazil report — which included messages and an audio from the senator to his 'brother' Daniel Vorcaro — appear disoriented by the revelation of his involvement with the controversial owner of Banco Master. The subscriber-only exposé has caused discomfort and uncertainty among his closest supporters, raising questions about his political viability.

item.title: Crusoé: O filme amaldiçoado sobre Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: The film Dark Horse, which portrays Jair Bolsonaro, faced financial difficulties and received a request for help from Flávio Bolsonaro to banker Daniel Vorcaro last year, according to an Intercept report. The production, featuring Jim Caviezel, sparked controversy and caused problems for Bolsonaro's supporters.

item.title: Filme sobre Bolsonaro enfrentou denúncias de agressão nos bastidores
item.description: The film 'Dark Horse', depicting Jair Bolsonaro's 2018 presidential campaign, faces allegations of assault, unpaid wages, and poor working conditions from crew members during filming in São Paulo. The accusations, compiled in a dossier by Sated-SP in December 2025, include claims such as actor Bruno Henrique's allegation of being attacked by security for bringing a cellphone onto the set. Funded with approximately R$ 61 million by businessman Daniel Vorcaro, the film is set to premiere on September 11.

item.title: Moraes se declara impedido e 1ª Turma do STF rejeita habeas corpus para Bolsonaro
item.description: The First Chamber of the Supreme Federal Court unanimously rejected a habeas corpus filed by a lawyer not part of Jair Bolsonaro's defense team, seeking to extend his house arrest beyond the 90 days granted by Alexandre de Moraes. Moraes recused himself from the vote, while Ministers Cármen Lúcia, Cristiano Zanin, and Flávio Dino ruled that the petition was inadmissible because the official defense had not authorized it and because Brazilian jurisprudence does not allow habeas corpus against judicial acts of a minister.

item.title: Flávio cai 13 pontos no Polymarket após divulgação de áudio enviado a Vorcaro
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) saw his 2026 presidential election odds drop 13 percentage points on Polymarket after the release of an audio in which he demanded payments from banker Daniel Vorcaro for the production of the film 'Dark Horse'. The audio, published by The Intercept Brasil, raised suspicions of financial irregularities tied to his pre-campaign.

item.title: Flávio já disse que família Bolsonaro não tinha "contato pessoal" com Vorcaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro previously denied having 'personal contact' with banker Daniel Vorcaro, but audio and messages revealed by The Intercept show direct conversations between them regarding the financing of the film 'Dark Horse', which received R$61 million from Banco Master. The messages include references to them as 'brothers' and occurred just days before Vorcaro's arrest and the liquidation of Banco Master, contradicting Flávio's statements to CNN. The case raises suspicions of private funds being used for political purposes, tied to Jair Bolsonaro's 2022 campaign.

item.title: PT vai cobrar CPI do Master e usar redes para associar fraudes a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The PT is planning to push for the installation of the Master CPI and use social media to link alleged frauds to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, following the release of audio in which he allegedly demanded over R$130 million from Daniel Vorcaro to finance a film about Jair Bolsonaro. The strategy aims to politically exploit the episode to damage the bolsonarist candidate's image in the 2026 elections.

item.title: Chrisóstomo diz que governo Lula “derrete” e cobra anistia ampla
item.description: Federal Deputy Coronel Chrisóstomo (PL-RO) stated that President Lula's government is 'melting' politically and advocated for the approval of the Amnesty PEC for those involved in the January 8, 2023, acts, proposed by the PL leader in the Chamber. He criticized the federal administration and called for broad amnesty for participants in the events.

item.title: PT prepara PowerPoint para detalhar relação de Flávio X Vorcaro
item.description: PT members plan to release a social media PowerPoint detailing the alleged relationship between Flávio Bolsonaro and businessman Daniel Vorcaro, involving R$61 million from Banco Master to fund the biopic 'Dark Horse' about Jair Bolsonaro. The 'BolsoMaster' strategy aims to link the case to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a 2026 presidential pre-candidate, after leaked audio showed discussions between him and Vorcaro about the film. The total negotiated amount was R$134 million, though no evidence confirms the full sum was transferred.

item.title: PT comemora áudio de Flávio com Vorcaro e aposta no "BolsoMaster"
item.description: PT members celebrated the leak of an audio in which Flávio Bolsonaro asks banker Daniel Vorcaro for sponsorship of a film about Jair Bolsonaro, viewing it as a political blow to the Bolsonaro campaign. The PT had previously prepared a strategy linking Flávio to the Banco Master scandal, using the slogan 'Banco Master é Bolso Master', and plans to use the audio to reinforce corruption narratives.

item.title: Interesse em terras raras mudou postura dos EUA ante o Brasil, diz vice-presidente de políticas da Americas Society
item.description: The U.S. interest in rare earths, driven by the threat of Chinese export restrictions, influenced the shift in American posture toward Brazil, according to Brian Winter of the Americas Society. He noted that the Lula-Trump meeting occurred strategically before Trump’s visit to Beijing and urged Brazil to act quickly to capitalize on its rare earth potential, despite bureaucratic delays that could extend project approvals up to ten years.

item.title: Governistas cobram CPMI do Master após suposto áudio de Flávio para Vorcaro
item.description: Government-aligned deputies intensified calls for a Parliamentary Inquiry Commission (CPMI) to investigate the Banco Master scandal following an alleged audio of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro requesting funds from banker Daniel Vorcaro to finance the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays Jair Bolsonaro’s 2018 campaign. According to Intercept Brasil, Vorcaro allegedly paid around R$61 million for the film, part of a reported R$134 million deal. Lawmakers accuse Congress of a 'big deal' to favor corrupt figures and grant amnesty to coup plotters.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia renuncia ao TSE um dia após posse de Kassio; Toffoli deve assumir vaga na corte
item.description: Minister Cármen Lúcia resigned from the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on Wednesday (13), one day after being replaced as president of the court by Kassio Nunes Marques. Her vacancy is expected to be filled by Minister Dias Toffoli, according to STF expectations.

item.title: A pesquisa Quaest ficou velha
item.description: The Quaest poll was quickly overtaken by news of Flávio Bolsonaro's involvement with Daniel Vorcaro, reported by Intercept Brasil. The seriousness of the allegations rendered the poll's data immediately outdated in the public discourse.

item.title: Vídeo feito com IA mostra Michelle beijando Moraes na boca e viraliza
item.description: An AI-generated fake video showing Michelle Bolsonaro kissing Alexandre de Moraes on the lips went viral on social media following the inauguration of Kassio Nunes Marques as TSE president. The montage was based on a real photograph of the two exchanging a greeting kiss and reignited concerns about malicious use of AI to produce false content involving public officials. The TSE has identified the spread of manipulated media as a key challenge for the 2026 elections.

item.title: “Financiamento político disfarçado de cinema”, diz petista sobre áudio de Flávio
item.description: The leader of the PT in the Chamber of Deputies, Pedro Uczai, stated that audio attributed to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro suggests political financing disguised as payment for the film 'Dark Horse', which portrays the senator's political trajectory. He demanded an immediate investigation, calling it a potential slush fund scheme. The allegation raises suspicions of illicit use of private funds to benefit a pre-campaign effort.

item.title: Empresário confirma que marcou reunião de Flávio Bolsonaro com Vorcaro
item.description: Businessman Thiago Miranda confirmed he scheduled a meeting between Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) and banker Daniel Vorcaro for December 11, 2024, at Vorcaro’s residence in Brasília, but stated the senator did not attend. Miranda testified before the Federal Police in the Banco Master investigation and said he does not recall any other meeting between the two. The Intercept Brasil initially reported the scheduling but did not confirm whether the meeting took place.

item.title: A próxima medida cara de pau do governo Lula
item.description: The Lula government announced a provisional measure to mitigate rising gasoline prices, just one day after Petrobras signaled a forthcoming increase. The move follows the repeal of a tax on 'blusinhas' (cheap clothing) that the government itself had introduced, drawing criticism for policy inconsistency.

item.title: Caiado promete enquadrar facções como terroristas no 1º dia de governo
item.description: Former Goiás governor and presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) announced that, if elected, he would classify criminal organizations as terrorist groups on his first day in office and deploy the Armed Forces to combat organized crime. The statement was made on social media on March 13, 2025. Caiado aims to position himself as a hardline candidate on public security.

item.title: MPT abre investigação para apurar fala de Zema sobre trabalho infantil
item.description: The Labor Public Ministry (MPT) has opened an investigation against former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) over statements suggesting the expansion of work opportunities for children. The probe was initiated following a complaint by the Parliamentary Front for Combating Child Labor after Zema said in an interview that 'every child can help with simple tasks'. Although he later revised his stance to focus on adolescents and apprenticeship programs, the original remarks sparked widespread backlash.

item.title: Ao vivo: governo anuncia novas medidas para combustíveis
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva announces new measures to mitigate the impact of war on Brazil's fuel sector. The announcement takes place at 3 p.m. at the Ministry of Mines and Energy, with the presence of Ministers Alexandre Silveira (Mines and Energy), Bruno Moretti (Planning and Budget), and Executive Secretary of Finance, Rogério Ceron.

item.title: Após reunião com Fachin, Flávio Bolsonaro promete ‘bonança’ entre instituições
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro met with Supreme Court Minister Edson Fachin to promote institutional dialogue and prevent rumors about him, stating he seeks peace to focus on Brazil’s problems. He said that if elected, there will be a period of 'bonanza' between institutions, with mutual respect for each branch’s sphere. While praising Fachin as balanced, he maintained harsh criticism of Minister Alexandre de Moraes, accusing him of persecuting his father, Jair Bolsonaro.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz acreditar na inocência de Ciro Nogueira ‘até que se prove o contrário’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) said he believes in the innocence of Senator Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI) until proven otherwise, noting that Nogueira, a former Minister of Civil House, has a fair rapporteur at the Supreme Court and a chance to defend himself. The Federal Police accused Nogueira of receiving improper benefits from banker Daniel Vorcaro in exchange for congressional assistance, including monthly payments, corporate acquisitions, international trips, and use of a property. Flávio also denied any involvement of his campaign’s communications coordinator, Marcello Lopes, with Banco Master, calling the claim a lie.

item.title: Flávio se reúne com Fachin no STF: “Fiquei com excelente impressão dele”
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) met with Minister Edson Fachin, president of the STF, in an institutional meeting. He said he was left with an 'excellent impression' of the magistrate and emphasized that he requested the visit.

item.title: Perfil feminino para vice de Flávio Bolsonaro perde força no PL
item.description: The profile of a woman for Flávio Bolsonaro’s ticket has lost strength within the PL, despite initially being seen as ideal by party president Valdemar Costa Neto. The campaign now prioritizes urgently attracting a Centrão party to the base, increasing the likelihood of a male vice-presidential pick. Senator Teresa Cristina (PP-MS) remains viewed as the ideal choice for the vice-presidential slot, even as the focus shifts.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro se reúne com Fachin e fala em ser mais propositivo e não reagir a provocações
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) met with Supreme Court President Minister Edson Fachin in Brasília for an institutional visit. He stated he aimed to present himself as a pre-candidate for president with a centrist, proactive profile, avoiding reactions to provocations and emphasizing respect for institutions and a forward-looking approach. Flávio denied discussing dosimetry or any ongoing STF rulings, describing the meeting as amicable and focused on pleasantries.

item.title: Pacheco reforça ao PT que não será candidato ao governo de Minas Gerais
item.description: Senator Rodrigo Pacheco (PSB) informed PT leader Edinho Silva that he will not run for governor of Minas Gerais in 2026, citing personal reasons and a possible exit from politics after his term. However, PT militants in the state still hope President Lula will convince him to run, especially after Pacheco suggested two alternatives: Josué Gomes and Jarbas Soares. The decision is not seen as final, as Edinho Silva plans to revisit the conversation with Pacheco.

item.title: Reação de Lula reforça leve favoritismo na eleição
item.description: Lula remains in a technical tie with Flávio Bolsonaro in second-round simulations, but his approval rating has stopped declining and shown signs of recovery, particularly following recent government actions. Despite persistent headwinds like inflation and indebtedness, measures such as repealing the 'blusinhas' tax, fighting organized crime, debt renegotiation, and diesel subsidies have strengthened his position. The outlook suggests a slight advantage for Lula, though the outcome may hinge on factors beyond his control, such as ongoing investigations.

item.title: Presidente do PT no Rio posa com arma e camiseta de Lula
item.description: The president of the PT in Rio de Janeiro, Diego Zeidan Quaquá, posted a photo holding a rifle at a shooting range while wearing a Lula-branded shirt, declaring himself a follower of revolutionary figures like Che Guevara and Marighella. The image was later deleted after public backlash. He is the son of Maricá’s mayor and national PT vice-president Washington Quaquá, who faced criticism within the party for defending the innocence of the Brazão brothers, later convicted in the murder of Marielle Franco.

item.title: Ao vivo: STF julga igualdade salarial e alcance da Maria da Penha
item.description: The Brazilian Supreme Court is ruling on Wednesday on the constitutionality of Law 14.611/2023, which requires companies with 100 or more employees to disclose salary reports and remuneration criteria to ensure gender pay equality. The Court will also decide whether protective measures under the Maria da Penha Law can be applied in gender-based violence cases absent a domestic, familial, or affective relationship between victim and aggressor, with general repercussion recognized.

item.title: Em aceno ao governo, Motta decide colocar em apreciação o PL do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta decided to put the bill ending the 6x1 work schedule to a vote, following the Lula government’s submission of the proposal with constitutional urgency. Initially viewed with skepticism by opposition-aligned lawmakers as an attempt by Lula to claim ownership of an idea already under legislative discussion as a PEC, the bill will now proceed in parallel with the constitutional amendment, deemed complementary to align legislation with forthcoming constitutional changes.

item.title: Explosão causada pela Sabesp vira munição eleitoral para Haddad em SP
item.description: A gas explosion caused by Sabesp in Jaguaré, which left one dead and three injured, was used by Fernando Haddad as electoral ammunition against Tarcísio de Freitas’ government, linking Sabesp’s privatization to rising tariffs, complaints, and profits. Haddad claimed privatization benefited only buyers while the public bore the costs, citing unfulfilled promises of lower tariffs. Governor Tarcísio called an emergency meeting and pledged compensation and accountability, while PT lawmakers condemned privatization as a Bolsonarist legacy harming the people.

item.title: O acordo de Motta com o governo para votar a PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: Chamber of Deputies President Hugo Motta announced that the House will advance the government's bill to end the 6×1 work scale, following an agreement with the Executive. The text will address sector-specific details and complement a constitutional amendment proposal (PEC) on the issue. The measure aims to reform working hours in specific sectors, with ongoing negotiations between branches of government.

item.title: Oposição apoiará fim da ‘taxa das blusinhas’ de Lula
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Chamber, Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB), announced support for the Provisional Measure that eliminates the 'blusinhas tax' of 20% on international purchases up to US$50, signed by Lula. He stated the measure results from popular pressure and opposition action, not as government support, but as a victory for the Brazilian people. The MP is valid for up to 120 days and requires congressional approval to become permanent law.

item.title: Quaest: 60% avaliam reunião de Lula e Trump como positiva
item.description: The Genial/Quaest poll conducted from May 8 to 11, 2026, reveals that 60% of Brazilians view the Lula-Trump meeting at the White House positively, considering it beneficial for Brazil. 43% believe Lula emerged politically strengthened from the encounter, and 37% see a positive impact on his image. The survey also shows increased support for alignment with the U.S., rising from 43% in April to 56% after the meeting.

item.title: Democrata, ex-PMB, lança brigadeiro da reserva como pré-candidato a presidente
item.description: The Democrata party, formerly the Brazilian Women's Party (PMB), launched the presidential pre-candidacy of Brigadeiro Átila Maia on March 12, 2026, a figure associated with the military reserve. The candidacy positions itself in the center-right with a nationalist platform, aiming to capture votes in an already crowded field of ideologically similar candidates.

item.title: Real é 2ª moeda que mais se valoriza durante conflito no Oriente Médio
item.description: The Brazilian real appreciated 5.09% against the U.S. dollar since the start of the Middle East conflict on February 28, marking the second-largest gain among 27 currencies analyzed, behind only the Israeli new shekel (8.28%). This appreciation was driven by rising oil prices, which boosted exports and dollar inflows into Brazil, combined with the central bank's contractionary monetary policy that maintained high real interest rates and attracted foreign capital. The stronger real also improves public finances through increased royalty revenues.

item.title: Messias agradece presidente da OAB por fala em posse no TSE
item.description: Attorney General of the Union Jorge Messias thanked OAB President Beto Simonetti for mentioning him during the swearing-in of Minister Kassio Nunes Marques as president of the TSE on Tuesday, May 12, 2026, in Brasília. Simonetti highlighted Messias while greeting the Brazilian legal profession, which was met with applause from attendees. The ceremony took place weeks after the Senate rejected Messias’s nomination to the STF, a major political setback for President Lula’s government.

item.title: STF AO VIVO – Lei da Igualdade Salarial e ampliação da Lei Maria da Penha – sessão de 13/5/2026
item.description: The STF is set to rule on the constitutionality of the Pay Equality Law (Law 14.611/2023), which mandates salary transparency in companies with over 100 employees, as well as whether the Maria da Penha Law applies to gender-based violence outside familial or affective contexts and the inclusion of inflation adjustments in judicial deposit corrections. The court will also consider ADPF 881, seeking to prevent the criminalization of prosecutors and judges for interpretive prevarication.

item.title: Fim da “taxa das blusinhas” não melhorará popularidade de Lula, diz oposição
item.description: The leader of the opposition in the Chamber of Deputies, Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB), stated that the revocation of the 'blusinhas tax' will not improve President Lula's popularity, arguing that the public will realize the same government that created the measure is now repealing it without addressing real issues.
